variants.headline: Looking back: grant programme passes over needy districts
variants.sub: Districts in need were passed over by a government grant programme.
variants.body:
We return to {first_reported}. Our report recorded this: A government grant programme had passed over districts that needed it.

Our movement believes public provision should be judged by the purpose it is meant to serve. Need is not a decorative word for a programme's description. A political argument about grants should keep the overlooked districts at its centre rather than treating an allocation as virtuous simply because money was authorised.

The event remains part of the record. Whether subsequent developments met the standard it raised is a separate question, not something the old headline can answer by itself.

We judge {target} adversely. Public grants deserve an allocation that takes need seriously, and passing over the districts that needed support is a proper reason to question the fairness of stewardship.
